rendered: Identification of the target. Using transposon mutagenesis, Pan et al. pinpointed the peptidoglycan synthase DacA as a negative regulator of prodigiosin biosynthesis, and the corresponding reference frames the finding as a loss-of-function effect:[1]Loss of serine-type D-ala-D-ala carboxypeptidase DacA enhances Prodigiosin production in Serratia marcescens[2]Effect of the knockout. The deletion acted on cell envelope properties and on the pathway's own gene expression:peptidoglycan synthase DacA as a negative regulator. Knocking out dacA in strain SK4–72 altered cell morphology and increased membrane permeability, facilitating intracellular prodigiosin release and upregulating pigA, resulting in a 2.46-fold yield increase over wild-type JNB5–1[3]The strain carrying the deletion. The knockout strain is[4]SK4–72[5], derived from the wild-type parentJNB5–1[6]. In[7]Table 2[8]this entry is listed with the strategy[9]Deletion of the negative regulator dacA to enhance prodigiosin[10]biosynthesis[11], in cultivation mode[12]shake flask[13], with a time in hours of[14]108[15]and a titer of[16]15,630[17]in the table's units of milligrams per litre.[18]
